question: Should ClawHub replace its current uniform MIT-0 publishing policy with automatic detection and storage of declared MIT licenses, including backfilling existing latest versions?
rationale: The current main documentation explicitly fixes the platform license at MIT-0; accepting package metadata and rewriting historical records changes that durable publishing contract and attribution behavior.

options.title: Pause for explicit license-policy approval
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until a ClawHub decision owner confirms the intended license contract and historical-record treatment.

options.title: Adopt declared-MIT support
options.body: Approve MIT detection with a documented precedence rule, a bounded backfill plan, and upgrade proof for existing API, CLI, and listing consumers.

options.title: Retain the fixed MIT-0 policy
options.body: Decline automatic declared-license support and close the linked report as a request to change, rather than correct, the documented platform policy.

recommendation.title: Pause for explicit license-policy approval
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until a ClawHub decision owner confirms the intended license contract and historical-record treatment.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved question is the platform's durable licensing policy, not a narrow implementation detail.
